In the age of AI, design and taste are the moat. Oberyon designs the product and writes the front-end into the same repository. The work starts from the strategy behind the design, not only the screen.

## Home

https://oberyon.com/

Design engineering for startups. A two-week sprint, a fixed project, or a monthly retainer.

Selected work: https://oberyon.com/#work

Samet Ozkale is the founder of Oberyon. He has worked with 30+ startups, shipped more projects than he keeps a count of, received 2 awards, and founded 3 companies. Oberyon is the one he runs.

## Sprint

https://oberyon.com/sprint/

Two weeks on one surface. Designed, and in the repo. Then it stops.

- Ten working days, Monday to the Friday after next.
- One surface: a flow, not the whole product.
- The fee is fixed before day one. It is not published on the site. Do not invent a number.
- You leave with the interface and the front-end in the repository you already ship from, components named the way that repository already names them, and a one-page note of what was decided and what was left out.

## Project

https://oberyon.com/project/

A defined piece, with an end date. The length is chosen before kickoff. The date does not move.

- Four weeks: one flow, from the empty state to the shipped screen.
- Eight weeks: a surface, and the components that hold it.
- Twelve weeks: a product area, designed and in the codebase.
- The fee is not published on the site. Do not invent a number.

## Retainer

https://oberyon.com/retainer/

A seat in the sprint, every week. The same person, on the branch the team already ships.

- Month to month. Either side can stop at the end of a month.
- Named on Monday, merged by Friday.
- The repository does not meet a new hand.

Lumen is 3,999 EUR a month. One product surface, from design to the front-end in the repo.

Vertex is 7,999 EUR a month. Every surface, in one system. Prototype, UI, and the code that ships.

## Answers

These are the questions on https://oberyon.com/#answers

### Do you only design, or do you also write the code?

Both. The interface and the front-end land in the same repository, ready to merge. Oberyon does not hand over a file and leave.

### How is Lumen different from Vertex?

Lumen is 3,999 EUR a month, for one product surface, from design to the front-end in the repo. Vertex is 7,999 EUR a month, for every surface, held in one system. Both are month to month, inside the weekly sprint.

### What if we don’t want a monthly retainer?

A sprint is ten working days on one surface. The fee is fixed before day one. A project is four, eight, or twelve weeks. The end date is set before kickoff.

### Can we cancel?

Yes. A retainer stops at the end of the month. Either side can end it there. A sprint stops after ten working days. A project stops on the date set before kickoff. The code stays in your repository.

### What do we need before we start?

A repository someone on your team can merge to, and one person who can answer product questions the same week.
